title: The generate-page CLI
question: How generate-page.mjs decides whether to write the page or exit with an error, and what a change request must preserve

intro.simple: The program reads the request, checks the data and writes the page only if everything is valid. It ends with a number: 0 when it wrote the page, 1 when data or scene is invalid, and 2 when something else failed.
intro.technical: The contract to preserve when changing this CLI is its three exit codes and error-line format (`field: what failed`, `scene:<line>: what failed`): the file header and `SKILL.md` describe them, and tests depend on them. Failure points are data validation (an extra or missing rule), scene validation (a word list over text, not a security barrier), and the entry point (`asProgram`), which has previously exited 0 without writing.

nodes.simple: Decides whether the file runs as a program or is only imported by another.
nodes.technical: `asProgram()` compares `import.meta.url` with the real path of `process.argv[1]`, obtained through `realpathSync` (486-488); the file's last line only calls `main` when it returns true (489). Without `realpathSync`, a symlink invocation (`install.sh --link`) returned false because Node resolves the link in one path but not the other (484-485): it exited 0 without writing. Failure point: silent failure reported as success. Trade-off: `catch` returns `false` when `realpathSync` throws, for example for a missing path, so nothing runs in that case either.

nodes.simple: The function that runs when the program is called: reads arguments and files, requests validation, writes the page and returns the exit code.
nodes.technical: `main(argv)` returns 0, 1 or 2 instead of exiting: its caller assigns the code to `process.exitCode` (489), and error lines go to the supplied `err`, which defaults to stderr (438). Reads arguments (439-459), data (461-466) and scene (467-470), validates (472-473), generates (475-476) and writes (477-480). Failure point: 1 (violated rule) and 2 (usage or read error) have different consumers; changing the chain can swap them.

nodes.simple: Checks all data at once and returns the list of errors without correcting anything.
nodes.technical: `validate(data, scene)` enforces schema 2 without stopping at the first failure and cross-checks `scene` views against the scene file: a `scene` view requires `--scene` (284) and a scene file requires a `scene` view (289). Finally, a scan looks for keys in text and field names (330-343). Trade-off: scanning everything gives the agent the full list in one pass, at the cost of a long function, lines 67 to 346. Each line collected by `fail` passes through `redact` (69), so none repeats a secret. Failure point: a missing rule accepts data the page template cannot draw; an extra rule rejects valid explanations.

nodes.simple: Checks scene code against a list of forbidden constructs over the entire text.
nodes.technical: `validateScene(code)` applies static rules to the entire text, not line by line: the 40 KB ceiling (352, 385-386), exactly one `function scene(` (388-391, 407-408), 32 forbidden words (355-370), including `window`, `document`, `globalThis`, `self`, `constructor`, `Reflect`, `opener` and `frames` (365), and patterns for `</script`, `<!--`, addresses, literal colors and `\u` and `\x` escapes (371-378). A match split across lines counts on its starting line, one per rule per line (349-351). Trade-off: scanning the whole text also catches comments and strings (rejects `location` in a comment) without needing a JavaScript parser; it rejects escapes everywhere because they could spell a forbidden word without it appearing in the text (376-378). Failure point: a forbidden-text list is not a security barrier: a word assembled from two strings (`"fe" + "tch"`) is absent from the text and passes.

nodes.simple: Puts data, title and scene inside the page template.
nodes.technical: `generatePage(data, { scene, template })` replaces the data block, `<title>` and, with a scene, its block (429-432). Escapes JSON's `<` (425) and the title (431). Replacements are functions so `$&` in data or scene is not interpreted as a pattern (421-422). Throws if the template lacks exactly one data block (426), the title marker (427) and, with a scene, exactly one slot (428). Failure point: a missing template marker is only detected here; `main` converts the error to exit 2 (475-476).

`readTemplate()` reads `assets/viewer.html`, located relative to the script folder (17-18), and turns read errors into a message containing the template path (417). It is the default for `generatePage`'s `template` parameter (424): the file is only read when the caller supplies no template, allowing a different template instead of the real one.

nodes.simple: The program checks what was requested.
nodes.technical: The `argv` loop accepts `--out` and `--scene` with a value not starting with `--` (443), rejects unknown options (455), a second data file (457) and repeated `--scene` (452), and requires a data file and `--out` (459). Repeated `--out` is accepted: the last wins (451). All failures here exit 2.

nodes.simple: The program opens the data file and, if present, the scene file.
nodes.technical: `read` only accepts a file, using `statSync(...).isFile()` (461): a directory exits 2, as does a read error, which reports the path and reason (462, 468). Invalid JSON exits 2 with only “<path> is not valid JSON”: a `JSON.parse` error would quote part of the file, and data must not enter a log (464-466). Without `--scene`, `scene` remains `null` (467).

nodes.simple: The program checks data and scene before writing.
nodes.technical: Collects lines from `validate` and, with a scene, `validateScene` (472). If any exist, writes each through `err` and returns 1 (473), before reading the template (475-476), `mkdirSync` or `writeFileSync` (478-479): the output file is neither created nor touched.

nodes.simple: The program opens the ready-made page.
nodes.technical: Happens inside `generatePage`, through the default `template = readTemplate()` (424). An unreadable template (417), missing markers (426-427) or missing scene slot (428) yields exit 2 (476), after data has passed validation (472-473).

nodes.simple: The program saves the page to the requested destination.
nodes.technical: Recursive `mkdirSync` for the destination folder and `writeFileSync` for the page (478-479). Reached only with valid data (472-473); write failures exit 2 (480). Writing is not atomic: it goes straight to the destination without a temporary file; failure midway can leave an incomplete file.
`main` returns 0 (481) and `process.exitCode` becomes 0 (489). The caller (the agent) proceeds to the detector (`SKILL.md`, step 4).

nodes.simple: Data or scene is invalid; nothing was written.
nodes.technical: One line per violated rule on stderr (`field: what failed` or `scene:<line>: what failed`), without writing anything (5-8, 472). The caller corrects data or scene and retries (`SKILL.md`, step 3); this is not an environment error.

nodes.simple: Something outside the rules failed: an argument, a file (including unreadable JSON), the template or writing.
nodes.technical: Usage or read error (8). Comes from arguments (439-459), reading data (463), invalid JSON (464-466), scene (469), template (476) or writing (480); the message identifies which. The caller corrects the command, file, template or writing, not the data rules. Only unreadable JSON requires rewriting data; the message does not identify where it fails.

steps.title: Who calls whom
steps.simple: Three floors: entry, checking and writing. Only the entry talks to the other two.
steps.technical: The end of the file (489) calls `main` only if `asProgram` returns true. `main` calls `validate` and, with a scene, `validateScene` (472), then `generatePage` (476), which reads the template by default (424). All synchronous: reads with `readFileSync` (461) and writes with `writeFileSync` (479). Validation functions receive data and scene as arguments (67, 381), so importers can call them without creating processes.

steps.title: The entry runs only as a program
steps.simple: The file also exports its functions, so it runs on its own only when called as a program.
steps.technical: The guard compares `import.meta.url` with the `realpathSync` of `process.argv[1]` (486-488). Through a symlink, without `realpathSync`, the guard returned false and the file exited 0 without writing (484-485); a test prevents recurrence (1118-1125). Changing the guard without keeping that test reopens the defect, hidden by exit 0.

steps.title: validate: all at once, without correcting
steps.simple: Checking does not stop at the first error: it returns the full list, so the agent can fix everything in one pass.
steps.technical: Each rule appends its line through `fail` (68-69) instead of stopping; `errors` is returned only at the end (345). Trade-off: the full list saves iterations, but each rule must remain independent. Changing a rule requires changing its test; `assets/examples/` examples must remain valid (1296-1298).

steps.title: validateScene: reject across the entire text
steps.simple: The 3D drawing's code passes a list of forbidden constructs before entering the page.
steps.technical: The list (32 words, addresses, `</script`, `<!--`, literal colors, `\u` and `\x` escapes, 40 KB) runs over the entire text, not line by line (349-351). Rejects more than strictly dangerous constructs (comments and strings), yet cannot prevent everything: a word assembled from two strings (`"fe" + "tch"`) is absent from the text. It is not a security barrier; the template's CSP restricts the page's network access (fixed by a test). Adding a word means adding a list entry (356-365); removing one allows the scene to use what was forbidden.

steps.title: generatePage: replace without interpreting patterns
steps.simple: The program inserts data into the ready-made page as it stands, without interpreting it.
steps.technical: `replace` replacements are functions, so `$&`, `$1` and `$'` in data or scenes remain literal (429-432). JSON's `<` is escaped so a `</script>` in text cannot close the block (425). Three `throw` statements (426-428) report missing template markers; an unreadable template throws in `readTemplate` (417).

steps.title: The CLI lifecycle
steps.simple: The program always follows the same steps in this order: arguments, files, checking, template, writing.
steps.technical: Each state advances only if the previous one succeeded. Order matters: validating (472-473) before reading the template (475-476) keeps data defects distinct from template defects, and ensures exit 1 never creates the file.

steps.title: Where exits 1 and 2 originate
steps.simple: 1 means “correct data or scene”; 2 means “something around them failed”.
steps.technical: Exit 1 comes only from validation (472-473) and leaves the destination untouched. Exit 2 has several sources: arguments (439-459), reading data and scene (461-470), template (475-476) and writing (480). CLI callers handle them differently: respond to 1 with corrected data or scene; to 2 with a corrected command, file or environment (rewrite data only if JSON is unreadable). The file header (5-8), `SKILL.md` and tests depend on these codes.

concepts.simple: If data or scene has errors, the program leaves nothing new on disk.
concepts.technical: With exit 1, the output file is neither created nor touched because `mkdirSync` and `writeFileSync` follow validation (the “Validate” and “Write” nodes). With exit 2 from arguments, reading or template, nothing has been written either; with exit 2 from writing, the destination may be incomplete.

concepts.simple: The scene is read as text without understanding it as code.
concepts.technical: `validateScene` does not parse JavaScript: it uses regular expressions over the entire text with identifier boundaries, including comments and strings.
